---
title: Which kind of app?
description: "The patterns for offering something to the platform: a packaged analysis tool, a device driver, an app inside your own program, a workflow that orchestrates others, an app served over HTTP, and a microcontroller. Which one fits, and what each looks like."
type: concept
---

An **app** offers something: actions that others can call, and often state they can watch. It
connects as an [agent](/docs/about/terminology#agent), registers what it offers and waits for
tasks. Every app is declared the same way, whatever the language (see
[Shared concepts](/docs/build/shared-concepts)). What differs is where it runs, who starts it and
what else it has to live with.

If your program only *uses* the platform (uploading data, starting tasks, reading results), it is
not an app in this sense. See [Connect to the platform](/docs/build/connect) instead.

## Which pattern?

| Pattern | Use it when | Runs | Started by | UI |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Plugin](/docs/build/apps/plugin) | You wrote an analysis tool, a model or a converter that others should install | in a container, on a server or a lab machine | the platform (Kabinet) | bloks |
| [Device](/docs/build/apps/device) | Your code drives hardware: a stage, a camera, a pump, a robot | on the machine the hardware is plugged into | you, or a system service | bloks |
| [Inside your own program](/docs/build/apps/host-program) | A program with a life of its own should also be callable: a Qt or napari GUI, microscope software, Fiji | inside that program's process | the program | the program's own, plus bloks |
| [Workflow](/docs/build/apps/workflow) | Your code calls other apps' actions and must survive a crash halfway | anywhere, usually as a plugin | the platform or you | bloks |
| [Served over HTTP](/docs/build/apps/http) | You want the same actions behind a plain HTTP API, with or without an Arkitekt server | inside a web server | your web server | none, or OpenAPI docs |
| [Microcontroller](/docs/build/apps/microcontroller) | The device has no computer, only a board | on the board, without an OS | power on | bloks |

These combine. A device app is often packaged as a plugin once it is stable. A Qt app can offer a
workflow. The patterns describe where an app lives, not what kinds of actions it may have.

## Three questions

1. **Does the code need something only one machine has?** Hardware, a licence, a GUI session, a
   running program. Then it is a [device](/docs/build/apps/device) or lives
   [inside your own program](/docs/build/apps/host-program), on that machine. Otherwise it can be a
   [plugin](/docs/build/apps/plugin) that runs wherever there is room.
2. **Does it call other apps?** Then those calls belong in a
   [workflow](/docs/build/apps/workflow), not a plain action.
3. **Who owns the process?** If Arkitekt should start, stop and update it, make it a plugin. If
   another program owns the process and the event loop, embed the app in it.

## What every pattern shares

- **The declaration.** An `App` with an identifier, a version and what it offers. It does no I/O.
- **The login.** The first time an app connects, a person approves it for their organization. The
  session is kept, so later runs connect on their own.
- **Outbound only.** An agent dials out to the server and opens no port, so it runs unchanged
  behind a lab firewall, in a container or on a microcontroller.
- **The rules on [Anti-patterns](/docs/build/anti-patterns).** State is small and actionable, UIs
  bind to it, large data travels by reference.

## Language support

| Pattern | Python | Rust | Kotlin |
|---|---|---|---|
| Plugin | yes, with `arkitekt plugin` | build your own image | not yet |
| Device | yes | yes | yes, no startup hooks yet |
| Inside your own program | yes: `run_detached`, Qt | yes | yes: what it was built for (Fiji) |
| Workflow | yes | not yet | not yet |
| Served over HTTP | yes: FastAPI | yes: axum | no |
| Microcontroller | no | yes: `no_std` on embassy | no |
